full_judgment:
6. An affidavit-in-opposition has been filed by the respondent Nos. 10 and 14 contending, inter alia, that the lands shown to have been sold in auction were beds of rivers and khal at the relevant time. These have been in use by the local public from time immemorial. The lands are public easement. These lands ought to have been recorded in government Khas Khatian No. 1 as non-retainable khas land of private landlords within the ambit of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Due to either inadvertence of settlement officials or fraud of the private landlords Nripendra Nath Ghosh and others, the lands were recorded in their names most illegally. Taking advantage of such illegal omission and the absence of the private landlords Mr. ATM Nurul Islam, husband of the petitioner, who was posted at Dumuria as the Engineer, Public Health Department at the relevant time, "brought to bear unholy influence on the local Revenue Officer of Dumuria and got the land sold in auction in a certificate case beyond the knowledge of the public at large by suppression of notices and proclamations". He purchased the land in the name of his wife and after obtaining certified copies, managed to make the records of the Certificate Case disappear with a view to concealing fraud and forgery. The petitioner got her name mutated in the SA Khatian beyond the knowledge of the public and abstained from payment of rent to conceal her auction purchase from the local public and the petitioner preferred an appeal against the impugned judgment and order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Khulna and others and also filed Title Suit No. 181 of 1986 on 29-5-86 in the 1st Court of Munsif which on transfer to the court of Additional Assistant Judge, Khulna, was renumbered as Title Suit No. 96 of 1990 for declaration that the order of Additional Deputy Commissioner, Revenue setting aside the auction sale (Annexure-C) in this writ petition was void, illegal and for permanent injunction. The suit was dismissed on contest by judgment and decree dated 27-3-90 and 3-4-1990 respectively with the findings, inter alia, that the suit land were river and canals, that some of the plaintiffs were minor at the time of alleged auction purchase and the auction sale was in contravention of Ordinance No. 1 of 1964 and the plaintiff (petitioner in this writ petition) failed to prove her title or auction purchase and possession of the suit land. Certified copy of the Judgment and Decree is annexed to the-affidavit-in- opposition and marked as Annexure-1 and 2 respectively. The petitioner preferred Title Appeal No. 88 of 1990 against the said judgment and decree but the appellate Court was pleased to allow withdrawal of the application of the petitioner by order No. 21 dated 16-6-93. Certified copy of the memorandum of appeal and withdrawal order are annexed to the affidavit-in-opposition and marked as Annexure 3 and 3(a) respectively. 

 7. It is submitted by the respondents that the river plot No. 139 which as claimed by the petitioner was leased out as Sairat Mohal by the Fisheries Department to Goalba Mutibari Matshajibi Samabaya Samiti in 1393 BS vide DCR No. 59477 dated 6-3-85 and DCR No. 6 dated 2-7-86. This river was also leased out in 1388 BS vice DC No. 432811 dated 8-8-88. Therefore the petitioner could not have acquired any ownership in Government khas land of public easement by virtue of a fraudulent and illegal sale. These documents he says were deposited by the respondents in VP Case No. 173 of 1987 (Khulna) of Bhumi Appeal Board which he could not take back due to unavoidable circumstances. A supplementary affidavit-in-opposition on behalf of the respondent Nos. 10 and 14 was filed annexing and among others certified copies of CS Khatian No. 2 marked as Annexure 4 -4(1). CS and Map prepared by the Government in 1922-23 in respect of Mowza Balabunia No. 127, Sheet No.2 covering the disputed lands clearly showing constitute the bed of some rivers and navigable canals marked as Annexure 5.
